name: Death of Muhammad and Early Caliphate
summary: Muhammad dies in Medina after unifying most of Arabia under Islam. The question of succession (khalifa = caliph) creates immediate controversy. Abu Bakr becomes the first caliph; his two-year reign suppresses tribal apostasy wars (Ridda Wars) and launches the first Islamic conquests of Byzantine Syria and Sassanid Persia. The speed of expansion suggests a powerful combination of military skill, religious motivation, and Byzantine-Sassanid exhaustion.

_quarry.structural_significance: The establishment of the caliphate creates the model of Islamic governance that shapes Muslim political thought to the present; the rapid conquests transform the political map from Spain to India within 100 years.
